title: How it Started vs How it's Going - My Art Improvements and Workflow for my Bug Auto-Battler
author: FabulusGames
selftext:
BugTeam Battles is a browser game built on Three.js. Claude Code writes a headless Blender (bpy) script for each species against a shared modeling and rigging library: rigid parts on one skeleton, 11 animation clips defined as functions of time, and four LODs from about 1.6k to 25k tris, exported as GLB. Subagents gather reference photos and scientific descriptions of each animal before the build. Textures are a multi-view ComfyUI repaint with a brush LoRA, run on Modal and projected back to UV, then a cleanup pass restores markings the diffusion step washes out. The map art was generated with Codex.

  
Play for free at [www.bugteambattles.com](http://www.bugteambattles.com)

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body: Slow down on those projectiles from the velvet worm; maybe add an arch for it. Because right now it looks like they're storm troopers blasting away with laser guns. But hey, it all depends on the style. If you want to go that route then it might be fine, but I'm confused in your game's approach because it seems like you're aiming for a realistic rendition of bugs, but yet they're shooting things in a cartoony way.

replies.author: FabulusGames
replies.body:
I appreciate the feedback. The goal is to keep the appearance of the bugs as close to reality as possible. However, their abilities and trait effects are only loosely based on their biology, some more so than others.   
  
That being said, the ability animations definitely still need some work. For the velvet worm in particular, it actually does spray it's slime incredibly fast, but the current animation still needs refining.

replies.author: Xinnobun
replies.body: Theres potential for a lot of unique balancing strategies, for instance spiders can disable one bug (wrap them up with their web) exceptionally well, however their influence in the battlefield is limited because they're primarily a single target DPSer as oppose to other bugs that are capable of AOE.

replies.author: FabulusGames
replies.body: Absolutely. The spider trait currently draws webs on the ground that can slow/stun units. If you go to [www.bugteambattles.com](http://www.bugteambattles.com) and click on "Field Guide" it shows all of the units, traits, and abilities.
